title: Bengal Famine
subtitle: Mass starvation, administrative failure, and social collapse under colonial rule.
summary: The Bengal Famine of 1943 caused catastrophic hunger and death across Bengal. Wartime disruption, inflation, grain-market failures, and policy breakdown under British colonial administration intensified the crisis, devastating rural households and urban poor communities alike.
heroTagline: In 1943, hunger became a political rupture in Bengal's history.
whyItMatters: The famine reshaped public trust in governance, sharpened anti-colonial anger, and left deep social scars that influenced Bengal's later political trajectory.
